images.caption: The town of Pullman was built in 1880-1885 on the plans of architect Solon S. Beman, with the  intent of creating superior living conditions for the employees of the Pullman Palace Car Factory. 85 different façade designs were built, each with specific door, window, porch, roof, and masonry details. Shared porches are common, as this pair of lovingly preserved homes illustrate. Several homes are open for touring in October each year.

images.caption:
A Black park ranger holds up a laminated black mustache up on a wooden stick to her lips and helps hold a a decorated frame that says "Pullman National Monument" with a visitor. The visitor, a Black middle-aged woman, stands close in the decorated frame and wears a striped blue and white shirt.
Labor Day 2019 celebrated women and their contributions to the labor movement in correlation. This visitor and a ranger enjoy a moment of silliness as they enjoy some of the selfie props provided at the event.

images.caption:
A blonde park ranger with blonde hair wearing a straw flat hat holds one side of a wooden award. On the other side, a taller black man holds the other side. He wears a blue t-shirt and black circle glasses. Both wear blue face masks.
Edgar Allan Poe Classical School was the recipient of our 2022 Pullman Partner Award for their amazing dedication to the park and the excellent work their students have done for the park. Principal Eric Dockery held the accepted the award on behalf of the school.

images.caption:
Two white men hold accordions in their hands outside standing on grass in front of a wooden band stand. Behind them, tree have just started to bloom with green leaves. 
The man on the left holds an accordion that is made of light-colored wood and blue and gold paper. He wears a traditional blue vest, blue face mask, and black fedora. The man on the right wears a blue jacket and red shirt. His accordion is a red wood accordion with purple and gold paper in the middle. He wears a dark blue patterned mask.
A yearly tradition in Pullman, the May Pole Dance welcomes in Spring. The dance, of course, also includes music!
Keywords: spring; may pole; traditions; community programs

images.caption:
A photo of a red brick row homes. Several of the homes have iron black fences along the front. Greenery peeks through the closest fence in the photo. The others have mowed grass front yards.
Many of the historic homes in Pullman have preserved facades that bring visitors back to the landscape of the 1880s. These homes, north of the Pullman industrial grounds, would have been more modest sized homes for the average worker.
Keywords: Pullman; Chicago; IL; Architecture; historic preservation

images.caption:
Three female park rangers pose together in front of a partially obscured mural on the back of a one-story building. The ranger on the left is a Black woman and the shortest of the three. She waves one hand and wraps her other hand behind the ranger next to her. She wears a National Park Service green ball cap and a grey mask. The middle ranger wears a straw flat hat with flowers on the brim. She is a white woman and wears a KN95 black mask. The ranger on the right is a white woman with long curly brown hair. She wears a green ball cap and a green face mask.
A yearly tradition in Pullman, the May Pole Dance welcomes in Spring.
